title: Independent review of the soundness argument
description: Every line was written in one session by a single author, and the soundness reasoning has had no reviewer. The mechanical trust boundary and the adversarial tests catch a producer lying; they do not catch the author reasoning wrongly about rounding. Two files carry essentially all the risk: interval.py (the nextafter widening argument) and backward_error.py (the rounding budgets ETA/GAMMA, the subnormal and overflow guards, and the bracketing argument).
acceptance_criteria: A second person has read interval.py and backward_error.py against the derivations in their docstrings and signed off or filed defects.

title: Emit a certificate from one real Krylov energy bound
description: Smallest end-to-end test. Pick one bound the solver already produces, wrap the eigenvector estimate and gap parameter as a witness, and run the checker. Expect the first attempt to fail: that failure is the finding.
acceptance_criteria: Checker returns VERIFIED or a specific ABSTAIN reason on a real solver output. Either outcome is a result; a crash or a schema mismatch is not.
close_reason: Bridge at chem/certkit_bridge.py emits a certificate from a real QKSD Krylov bound (H2/sto-3g, 16-dim qubit Hamiltonian, CSR backend). Final verdict VERIFIED, re-derived [-1.8523881735695890, -1.8523881735695755], exact value inside. Artifact re-checked standalone by certkit.cli on a Python where numpy does not import. Three findings filed.

title: Integrate certkit with the Krylov solver
description: The premise of certkit was a cross-project unifier. So far nothing emits into the format: the only producer is the synthetic one written alongside the checker. Until a real energy bound from the Krylov solver becomes a certificate that the checker either verifies or refuses, the design has not been tested against the thing it was built for.
acceptance_criteria: A certificate produced by the Krylov solver from a real problem instance, verified by an unmodified checker, with the verdict recorded.

title: Fix pre-existing type-class errors in Soundness.lean (inertia_count_below, weyl_shift)
description: Soundness.lean fails to compile as a whole due to two pre-existing type-class resolution errors unrelated to certkit-8y2.2's work: (1) inertia_count_below's hldl hypothesis uses 'L.BlockTriangular id' which needs an 'LT n' instance that isn't available for the generic Fintype/DecidableEq n in scope; (2) weyl_shift's conclusion uses '||A - B||' on Matrix n n R, which needs a Norm instance that Matrix n n R doesn't have by default in this mathlib revision (rev 67f608e6163ac30cf48c9c4b8f3e060a5588117e). Discovered while wiring Certkit.BackwardError into Soundness.lean for certkit-8y2.2 — that bead's real, zero-sorry theorem (sweep_backward_bound) compiles fine when checked directly via 'lake env lean Certkit/Soundness.lean' (the full build log ends cleanly after the line-105 weyl_shift error, with no further errors reported), but the file cannot be added to the default 'lake build Certkit' target until these two are fixed, most likely by adding an explicit LinearOrder/LT instance argument for inertia_count_below and picking the right norm instance (e.g. via Matrix.instNormedAddCommGroup or similar, or restating with a concrete norm like the Frobenius/operator norm helper mathlib provides) for weyl_shift.
acceptance_criteria: Both type-class errors resolved (or replaced with a documented alternative formulation); 'lake build Certkit' succeeds with Certkit.Soundness imported from Certkit.lean; no new sorry introduced beyond the 6 that already exist as intentional specification placeholders.

title: Coverage cliff: past DENSE_LIMIT the only route gives Ha-scale widths
description:
certkit-jn1.1/jn1.3 finding, now quantified on real molecular Hamiltonians via the Pauli backend:

  case  dim   route                width      chemical accuracy
  H2     16   temple_inertia       3.7e-09 Ha   ok
  H2     16   gershgorin_rayleigh  1.6e-01 Ha   100x too wide
  H4    256   gershgorin_rayleigh  7.9e-01 Ha   500x too wide
  N2   4096   gershgorin_rayleigh  2.6e+00 Ha   1600x too wide

Every one of these VERIFIES and every one contains the exact value, so soundness is intact and this is purely coverage. But past n = 160 the inertia route is gone, so the gap cannot be discharged, so Temple cannot be used, and the only surviving route is a Gershgorin floor whose width grows with the operator. Chemical accuracy is 1.6 mHa. Nothing above 16 dimensions is within three orders of magnitude of useful.

This is the concrete case for the README's 'a count rule that works matrix-free' item: it is what would let a large Pauli Hamiltonian use temple_ref instead of falling back to Gershgorin, and it is the difference between certkit being a demonstration and certkit being usable on the Krylov solver's real workloads.
acceptance_criteria: A counting rule that discharges the gap hypothesis without an O(n^3) dense factorisation, giving a Temple-quality width on a Pauli-sum operator of at least 256 dimensions.
notes:
Session 2 result: LEFT OPEN, no code changed. Continuation of the prior
session's negative result -- both of its explicitly-flagged open questions
were tested this session and both closed negative. Full writeup in
sandbox-handoffs/certkit-ph1.md (rewritten) plus two new scratch scripts.

Open question 1 (from session 1): does Variant A's global block-residual
eps=||AQ-QT||_2 shrink for a *genuinely gapped, low-entanglement* Hamiltonian
instead of critical TFIM? Tested: TFIM at field=0.3/1.0/3.0/8.0 (ferro,
critical, para, deep-para), q=10, k up to 80. Answer: NO -- eps/gap gets
*worse* as field increases (1.6e1 at critical -> 2.1 at deep-para is closer
but still O(1), while raw eps grows from ~5 to ~30 because ||A|| itself grows
with field). The obstruction is structural, not entanglement-related: eps
measures ||A|| restricted to Q's complement, which does not shrink just
because the target eigenvalue's gap is genuinely large.

Open question 2 (from session 1, explicitly untried): shift-invert Lanczos,
using the matrix-free Gershgorin floor (existing, sound,
certify_lambda_min_matrixfree's floor) as sigma so A-sigma*I is PSD and CG
applies without knowing lam1 in advance. Tested q=6/8/10, k up to 40 (numpy
prototype, dense CG standing in for a matrix-free solve). Answer: NO --
eps_spec stays O(1)-O(10), same order as plain Lanczos, and gets *worse* at
larger k for q=10 (CG ill-conditioning: Gershgorin sigma is 1.5x-2x further
from lam1 than the true spectral radius, so (A-sigma I) is poorly
conditioned). Shift-invert converges theta1 to lam1 well (confirms the
per-Ritz residual, i.e. Variant B's ingredient, is fine) but does NOT shrink
the block residual Variant A needs.

Conclusion this session: the failure is structural, not a subspace-choice
problem. ||AQ-QT||_2 small requires Q to capture essentially all of A's
"significant-norm" directions, not just an accurate ground-state estimate.
For an extensive many-body Hamiltonian (term count grows with system size,
spectral width does not shrink), no k<<n subspace -- Lanczos or
shift-invert -- satisfies that. Variant A is now believed to be a dead end
for this operator family specifically, not just under-explored. Variant B
remains explicitly UNSOUND (session 1's counterexample stands, not
retested).

Nothing in certkit/, tests/, or examples/ touched. Suite: 121 passed (current
tree baseline includes other beads' uncommitted work, not mine -- verified
unchanged by diffing before/after). No-dependency checker run still
verifies. Left claimed+open -- acceptance criterion (Temple-quality width,
matrix-free, >=256 dims) not met. Next session should try a fundamentally
different technique (polynomial/Chebyshev-filtered subspace, or question
whether the acceptance bar is achievable at all for generic local
Hamiltonians -- not yet established either way) rather than further
Krylov-subspace variants of Variant A, which are now twice-refuted.

title: Krylov sector scope does not survive translation to lambda_min_enclosure
description: certkit-jn1.1 finding. The solver's Temple bracket is certified against the lowest REACHABLE levels (temple_bounds.py honest-scope note); certkit's lambda_min_enclosure is a claim about the whole operator. Transcribed directly for H2/sto-3g the self-mode eps = -0.2320 Ha while the matrix's true lambda_2 = -1.2533 Ha, so the Temple premise eps <= E_1 fails by 1.02 Ha and the checker refuses: '13 eigenvalues lie below beta, need exactly 1'. Here the sector ground happened to coincide with the global lambda_min so the CLAIM was still true and only the PREMISE was wrong. On a molecule where a lower-lying sector exists, the same translation emits a claim that is false, not merely unproven.
acceptance_criteria: Either a sector-restricted claim kind that carries its subspace as part of the claim, or a documented producer rule that beta must separate the full spectrum and a full-space route for obtaining it.
notes:
RESOLVED. Constructed the deliberate adversarial case the prior notes asked
for: tests/test_sector_scope.py builds a 5-dim block-diagonal operator with
two decoupled sectors, where sector A's local ground/gap (self-mode eps=-1.0,
beta=1.0, mirroring the H2 case's shape) is NOT the global minimum (sector B's
ground is -4.0). A hand-built certificate submits exactly what a naive bridge
would: sector A's exact local eigenvector and local beta, translated directly
into a lambda_min_enclosure claim on the whole operator -- a *point* claim
[-1.0, -1.0], as confident as a false claim can look (residual is exactly 0
since the vector is an exact eigenvector of the block-diagonal operator).

check() abstains: "2 eigenvalues lie below beta, need exactly 1." Confirmed
this isn't magnitude-dependent (a 0.01 violation is still caught, not just
H2's dramatic 1.02 Ha one), and confirmed the contrast case (sector ground
IS the global min) verifies correctly with a padded claim. Also confirmed
certkit's own producer.certify_lambda_min on the SAME defeating matrix finds
the true minimum, because _ground_state always solves the whole operator,
never a sector -- demonstrating the acceptance criterion's "full-space route"
already exists in-repo.

Root cause of why this can never become a false VERIFIED: _rule_temple_inertia
/_rule_temple_ref discharge beta by inertia-counting eigenvalues of the actual
operator the certificate references (via op.interval_rows(), independent of
whatever subspace reasoning produced beta), not the producer's sector. A
sector-local beta that fails to separate the true full spectrum makes that
count come out != 1 and the rule abstains before Temple's arithmetic runs.
This was already true of the existing code -- no rule changed.

Satisfied acceptance criterion (b): documented the invariant explicitly in
README.md ("The guarantee" item 3, plus a new "Known limits" bullet) and in
checker.py's _temple() docstring, both pointing at the new regression test.
Did NOT implement acceptance criterion (a) (a sector-restricted claim kind) --
not needed given (b) is already mechanically enforced, and adding a claim kind
nothing in this repo produces would be speculative surface, not a fix.

Documented the invariant (README + checker.py docstring) and added a permanent regression test (tests/test_sector_scope.py). No code path in checker.py or producer.py changed.

title: Operator adapter for the solver's actual Hamiltonian representation
description: The Operator interface (apply, row, interval_rows) was designed against dense, CSR, and Pauli sums that I chose. The solver's representation may not fit it. If row access is unavailable the Gershgorin route dies; if entries are not exactly represented the backward-error route dies.
acceptance_criteria: Either the solver's Hamiltonian implements Operator, or a documented list of which rules it can and cannot support.
close_reason: Answered: the Pauli-sum backend fits the solver's representation exactly, CSR does not. qiskit SparsePauliOp -> encode_pauli needs only a label reversal (certkit is LSB-first, qiskit MSB-first); all molecular terms are real with even Y count, so PauliSumReal's realness precondition holds by construction. Materialising to CSR instead FAILS: summing Pauli terms in float makes (i,j) and (j,i) accumulate in different orders and H4 comes out asymmetric by 8.3e-17, which certkit refuses correctly. Verified end to end on H2 (16), H4 (256), N2 CAS(6,6) (4096). Note one coverage cost: Pauli interval rows are looser than exact CSR rows, so H2's inertia route now abstains on 'pivot straddles zero' where the CSR encoding got far enough to count eigenvalues. Both are abstentions; soundness unaffected.

title: Support the generalized eigenproblem Ax = lambda S x
description: Real quantum chemistry carries an overlap matrix. Every rule in the kit assumes the standard problem. Not a small extension: Rayleigh quotient, residual, Temple, and the inertia count all change, and the S-inner-product needs its own enclosure discipline.
acceptance_criteria: A lambda_min_enclosure rule for the generalized problem, with the same abstain-not-degrade behaviour, plus an exact-oracle test.

title: sandbox-prompt.md misdescribes Lean proof status: claims all 7 obligations are sorry and sweep_backward_bound is a bare True stub
description:
sandbox-prompt.md lines 56-62 ('Do not describe the Lean side as proved') state:

  'lean/Certkit/Soundness.lean states seven obligations against mathlib4 and every one ends in `sorry`. The file has never been compiled here. One of the seven, `sweep_backward_bound`, is currently stated as `True` -- the obligation with the worst failure mode is not yet even written down.'

CONFIRMED WRONG as of commit 39d6ff3 (2026-08-27), by reading lean/Certkit/Soundness.lean directly:

1. The file's own header docstring (lines 1-10) already says: 'Six of the seven theorems below are `sorry` ... The seventh, `sweep_backward_bound`, is a real, compiled, zero-`sorry` proof (see its own doc comment for exactly what it does and does not cover) -- do not read that as license to call the other six proved.'
2. The `sweep_backward_bound` theorem body (lines 146-152) is not `sorry` and not a bare `True`: it is a full statement discharged by `sweep_step_backward_bound hu hu1 h0 h1 h2 h3`, a real lemma imported from `Certkit.BackwardError` (formalized by certkit-8y2.2, which is closed).
3. The six theorems that remain `sorry`: rayleigh_ritz_min, residual_encloses_some_eigenvalue, temple_lower, inertia_count_below, gershgorin_lower, weyl_shift.

This traces to a real sequence of events: certkit-8y2.2 ('Formalize sweep_backward_bound') was closed and its work landed (commit 508caf2 'lean work' and later), which updated Soundness.lean's own header comment -- but sandbox-prompt.md's guardrail paragraph, which every future worker session reads verbatim as ground truth about the Lean file, was never updated to match. It is now describing a pre-8y2.2 state as current.

Why this is worth fixing rather than shrugging off as 'stale but harmless': this exact paragraph is the mechanism by which the standing prompt prevents a future session from either (a) overclaiming the Lean side is proved, or (b) wasting a session re-discovering that sweep_backward_bound needs formalizing when it already is done (duplicate work), or (c) missing that `weyl_shift`'s own doc comment (Soundness.lean lines 104-123) explicitly flags a real, currently-uncovered gap -- the relation between the entrywise/row-sum bound `sturm_be` actually computes at runtime and the `L2Operator` norm `weyl_shift` is stated against -- which is arguably now the more honest candidate for 'the obligation with the worst failure mode not yet even written down' than sweep_backward_bound, which is finished.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: rewrite sandbox-prompt.md lines 56-62 to match the live state of lean/Certkit/Soundness.lean at close time (re-grep for `sorry` in the file rather than hardcoding '6 of 7' -- certkit-8y2.3 and certkit-8y2.4 are in_progress and may change that count before this bead is picked up). The corrected paragraph should: (a) accurately state which theorems are sorry vs proved at the time of the edit, (b) not claim more progress than exists, and (c) not describe less progress than exists either -- both directions are a false claim about the thing this repo exists to be careful about, per the same paragraph's own stated standard.

No code, test, or certkit/ changes needed -- this is a documentation-only correction to the standing prompt template, not to certkit/ or lean/. No soundness surface.

title: Document that producers must pad claims against the checker's interval widening
description: certkit-jn1.1 finding. The checker re-derives in outward-rounded interval arithmetic, so its enclosure is strictly wider than any exact-float bound the producer computed. An unpadded transcription of a correct bound is therefore ALWAYS refused as 'tighter than the re-derived enclosure'. certkit.producer._pad encodes the right convention (relative slack plus an n-dependent term) but it is private and undocumented, so an external producer hits this immediately and has no guidance. This is the first thing any integrator will trip over and it looks like a soundness failure when it is a calibration requirement.
acceptance_criteria: _pad or an equivalent is public and documented in the README's producer-side notes, with the reason spelled out.
close_reason: pad_claim (formerly private _pad) is now public and documented in README's new 'Writing a producer' section; docstring expanded to name the mechanism (checker's outward-rounded re-derivation) it compensates for. Suite: 120 passed, 0 failed. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/certkit-kj6.md

title: Real-time Krylov witness is complex; the format is real-only
description: certkit-jn1.1 finding. QuantumKrylovSolver.eigenstates returns complex statevectors (real-time basis). certkit witnesses are real. For H2/sto-3g 53% of the state's weight sat in the imaginary part. H is real symmetric so its ground vector can be chosen real and either part is a usable trial vector, but the Rayleigh quotient of the real part is a DIFFERENT number than that of psi0 -- transcribing psi0's bracket with the real part as witness produces 'claimed interval is tighter than the re-derived enclosure'. The bracket must be recomputed on the vector the certificate actually carries.
acceptance_criteria: Either the bridge recomputes mean/variance on the emitted real witness (done in chem/certkit_bridge.py), or certkit-3ta complex support lands and the complex state is carried directly.
notes:

title: Emit certificates from the robot abstention layer
description: The other half of the cross-project claim. M0-M3 already build an interval substrate, IBP/CROWN bounds, and a branch-and-bound discrepancy certifier that produces a trusted epsilon. Routing it through this format makes the epsilon checkable, and turns each branch-and-bound subproblem bound into a referenced certificate rather than an internal number.
acceptance_criteria: A certified epsilon from the abstention layer verified by an unmodified certkit checker.
close_reason: Not executable from this repository, and not executable as specified by any future certkit-only session either. Confirmed the robot abstention layer / M0-M3 / IBP / CROWN / branch-and-bound-discrepancy code has never existed here: git log --all, find, bd search (robot/abstention/IBP/CROWN/discrepancy/cross-project), and bd memories all return nothing beyond the one README.md 'Where this connects' paragraph (aspirational vision text from the initial commit, never a pointer to an artifact). This is a stronger obstruction than certkit-bz5/certkit-487 hit for the chem bridge (a missing file): even if the robot-side code existed, the bead's own acceptance criteria requires verification by an UNMODIFIED checker, and checker.py's RULES table only knows eigenvalue/spectrum claims about a referenced linear operator (lambda_min_enclosure, lambda_min_upper_bound, eigenvalue_count_below, spectrum_lower_bound). IBP/CROWN branch-and-bound certifiers bound a (generally nonlinear) output margin over a box, not an operator's spectrum -- there is no existing claim kind to route that epsilon through without adding one, which would both violate 'unmodified checker' and repeat the 'speculative surface' new-claim-kind that certkit-487's handoff already declined to add for a better-specified case. Considered and rejected substituting the different SDP-relaxation eigenvalue technique (which would fit lambda_min_enclosure) -- that isn't IBP/CROWN and reporting it as such would misdescribe what was tested, the same anti-pattern this repo forbids in arithmetic applied instead to the connector story. Did not fabricate a synthetic bridge the way bz5 did for its bug, because bz5's bug had exact numeric specifics to reconstruct faithfully (a named Hamiltonian shape, a named 53% imaginary weight) and this bead's text gives no operator, no claim kind, and no numeric example to anchor a faithful reconstruction to -- anything built would be invented and presented as if representative of a system I cannot inspect. Made zero code changes. Full suite unchanged: 127 passed (uv run pytest tests -q). No-dependency checker run reconfirmed clean (numpy unimportable, examples/sample/certificate.json still VERIFIED via temple_inertia). See sandbox-handoffs/certkit-0vd.md for full investigation and citations.

title: Extend the backward-error analysis to bandwidth > 1
description: sturm_be is tridiagonal-only. The banded interval route still has to handle b > 1 and still gives out early. The per-step collection of rounding factors needs redoing for a band factorization.
acceptance_criteria: A banded sturm_be with the same runtime-delta discipline, and the delta-scales-with-the-operator test extended to it.

title: Exact-oracle testing beyond tridiagonal operators
description: The Fraction-based Sturm bisection is the strongest soundness evidence in the repo and it only covers one operator shape. It already caught a real disagreement: at n = 400 the certified enclosure is narrower than LAPACK error and eigvalsh falls outside it. Nothing comparable exists for banded, dense, or Pauli operators.
acceptance_criteria: An exact rational oracle for at least dense and banded operators, wired into the test suite.

title: Better eigensolver on the producer side
description: Counting is no longer the binding constraint; the producer's eigenvector is. Past n = 10^4 an unconverged Lanczos vector gives a large residual and Temple turns it into a useless-but-sound interval (width 1.6 at n = 10^4, 6e4 at n = 2e5). Shift-and-invert or LOBPCG would fix it. Pure coverage work with no soundness risk, which is exactly why it can wait.
acceptance_criteria: Certified width below 1e-9 at n = 10^5 on the Schrodinger fixture.
close_reason: Acceptance criterion met and pinned by test: tests/test_backward.py::test_ground_state_eigenvector_is_no_longer_the_binding_constraint asserts certified width < 1e-9 at n=100000 on the Schrodinger fixture (bead asked for below 1e-9); passes. _ground_state now routes tridiagonal encodings to LAPACK MRRR via scipy.linalg.eigh_tridiagonal (O(n), no dense materialisation), falling back to matrix-free Lanczos when scipy is absent -- producer-side solver choice, so a fallback costs coverage and never soundness. scipy added to the producer/dev extras only; the checker keeps dependencies = [] and the no-dependency CLI run is clean. NOTE: that worker session died before writing sandbox-handoffs/certkit-8q0.md, so there is no handoff for this bead -- the test and this reason are the whole record.

title: sandbox-prompt.md test-count/timing baseline is stale (says 106 passed, actual is higher)
description:
sandbox-prompt.md (the standing prompt fed to every worker session, checked into the repo root) states in two places:

  - line 66: 'The suite is **fully green**: `106 passed`. There is no documented pre-existing failure to excuse one.'
  - line 106: '  uv run pytest tests          # 106 passed, about 5 seconds'

README.md:448 also states '106 tests' in the file inventory table (the 'tests/' row of the directory listing).

CONFIRMED WRONG: on 2026-08-27 at commit 39d6ff3 (clean tree, no uncommitted changes), running the exact documented command:

    uv sync --extra dev
    uv run pytest tests -q

produced:

    154 passed in 18.17s

not 106 passed in ~5s. The gap (48 extra tests, ~13s extra) is almost certainly the accumulation of test files added by beads closed after the '106' baseline was written (e.g. test_generalized.py, test_complex_hermitian.py, test_sector_scope.py, test_composition.py, test_complex_witness_transcription.py all exist now and are plausibly newer than the baseline). This is not a test failure and not a soundness issue -- every one of the 154 passed -- it is purely a stale number in the guidance text that every future worker session reads as ground truth ('Known baseline -- do not mistake this for your own breakage').

Why this matters enough to fix: a future session comparing its own run against '106' has no way to tell 'tests were added since this baseline was written' apart from 'something is wrong with my environment'. Left uncorrected, it either causes false alarm or gets silently ignored (worse: normalizes ignoring the stated baseline).

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: re-run `uv sync --extra dev && uv run pytest tests -q` fresh at close time (more tests may have landed between filing and picking this up -- do not reuse the 154 number blindly, use whatever the live run reports) and update:
  - sandbox-prompt.md line 66 and line 106 to the live passed-count and rough wall-clock time
  - README.md:448's '106 tests' figure in the directory-listing table

No code, test, or certkit/ changes needed -- this is a two-file, three-line documentation correction. Low risk, no soundness surface at all.

title: Performance: the checker is pure Python
description: 60 seconds at n = 2e5 caps what anyone would run this on. A Rust or C core for the interval loops is the obvious move, but it enlarges the trusted base and the current implementation is auditable by reading, which has real value. Deliberate tradeoff, not an oversight.
